author: Good Enough
description:
Patients were dropped into freezing water, and doctors called it “treatment.”

In early insane asylums, cold water therapy was used as a method to control and “cure” patients. Some were locked in cages and submerged in ice-cold baths, while others endured hours-long exposure, freezing towel wraps, or the infamous “bath of surprise,” where patients were suddenly dropped into water without warning.

This video breaks down one of the most disturbing medical practices in history, how it was justified at the time, and what patients were forced to endure inside these institutions.
title: They Dropped Patients into Freezing Water 😰🌊 #history #medicalhistory #darkhistory #disturbing

author: Good Enough
description:
Patients were frozen, beaten, and locked away, and doctors called it “treatment.”

In early insane asylums, methods like cold water therapy, isolation cells, and brutal restraint devices were used to control patients. These practices were widely accepted at the time, despite causing extreme physical and psychological harm.

This video explores the most disturbing treatments in asylum history, how they were justified, and what life was really like inside these institutions.
title: Doctors Called This 'Treatment'... It Was Torture 😰💀 #didyouknow #history #darkhistory #disturbing
